I was really looking forward to Crimson Desert, but it ended up being a huge disappointment for me.

The only thing I genuinely enjoyed was the visuals. The world is beautiful, and the graphics are impressive, with some stunning landscapes that make exploration look appealing.

Unfortunately, that's where the positives end. The gameplay feels clunky and unpolished, and I never found the combat or mechanics particularly enjoyable. The story also failed to keep me engaged—it felt generic, with characters and quests that I quickly lost interest in.

What disappointed me the most is that the game feels like an MMORPG that was turned into a single-player game, rather than a true single-player RPG. Many of the quests, systems, and overall design have that MMO structure, which made the experience feel repetitive and lifeless instead of immersive.

Overall, despite its gorgeous graphics, I can't recommend it. A beautiful world isn't enough to make up for weak gameplay and an uninteresting story.

I had high hopes for this one from all the praise, and I had hoped for an interesting and rich world to explore and immerse myself in, but it lacks anything interesting to find or do.

The world looks fantastic and runs well on my high end system. It also does a great job of feeling alive and being a place where you want to spend time at first. The attention to detail is amazing, but you quickly discover that it is superficial, meaningless and repetitive. I rode through much of the map and the same NPCs and enemies are found everywhere, there is some variety but it is minimal. Same with the badly fitting voices and same repeated phrases.

The game is not bad, but it is bland and feels like busywork. The main story never engaged me, and I had hoped to just do side-quests and explore but quickly discovered that the side quests and the NPCs and posters that give these to you are typical, mundane and boring MMO tasks and fetch quests handed out by bland unmemorable NPCs. The enemies you fight in great numbers are just bland mobs of the same type. Orcs, people or the giants(?) all behave the same and have the same voices and are encountered everywhere the same. As if everything is blended together into a tasteless porridge, and with AI that at first impression seems immersive but is quickly revealed to be very simplistic. 

I do like the climbing and freedom to roam, but sadly the game does not allow you the freedom to interact meaningfully with the world beyond the bland and boring progression of story and faction quests and so I cannot recommend this.

If I were to give the game a single 'critique' (which I loosely say just due to the fact that I'm on my first playthrough, and I chose hard), it'd simply be how challenging combat is in boss battles compared to regular enemies. In Crimson Desert, you have enemies that can be interrupted, and enemies that can't be interrupted.

Enemies that are large (like giants), or bosses (all of them) cannot be interrupted and you have to time your strikes between theirs. You'll also need to know how to properly time your dodge and parry. claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game world features extensive open-world exploration, expansive scale, and visually impressive graphics.

citations.review_text: I love games like BG3 or KCD2, the open world RPG exploration and the way it makes you feel truly immersed as whatever character you're playing is hard to replicate but this game does it and does it so well. If you're big on RPG fantasy games, you'll love this.

I've been following this game since launch, and every update made me feel like the devs were actually listening to the community and trying to improve it. I still think it needs more work though, especially the controls and camera. They've gotten better, but if someone asked me whether it's worth playing right now, I'd still tell them to wait a bit.

The game does a lot of things well, but it also has a lot of problems. For every positive, there's usually a negative. Even then, the open world, the exploration, the interactivity, and the amount of content made me ignore a lot of the problems and enjoy what the game does well.

Every time I started playing, I had so many things I wanted to do that I didn't know where to begin. But then I'd notice something on the way and forget about all my plans. The world is designed in a way that always makes you want to see what's over there. Before I knew it, I was exploring somewhere completely different and forgot what I was going to do in the first place. Most of the time, I found something that made exploring worth it, and that's what kept me coming back.

If you like open-world games and exploration, I think you'll enjoy this game. But if you're mainly playing for the story, I don't think this is the right game for you.

Who should buy it: Players who value fluid combat and jaw-dropping exploration over narrative depth.

This is one of the most divisive games I have played, and for understandable reasons. It delivers some of the most impressive moments I've experienced in an open-world game, but those highs are offset by equally noticeable shortcomings. Whether you enjoy it will largely depend on how much you value exploration over storytelling and role-playing depth.

Pros!
* A vast open-world sandbox with light RPG elements that encourages exploration.
* Engaging world interaction mechanics, combat and skill systems that, while not particularly deep, are satisfying to learn and master.
* Multiple playable characters with independent skill progression provide good replay value.
* Exploration is consistently rewarding and is easily the game's greatest strength. CD has great draw distance that gives the world an exceptional sense of scale and nearly every location you can see is accessible, whether by walking, climbing, gliding, or flying.

Cons!
* The main story lacks cohesion, with questlines often feeling disconnected. This is particularly the case in the beginning of the game, where you are tasked to complete a random set of tasks without much explanation as to why these are important.
* Most side quests are simple fetch quests or promising ideas that rarely deliver a satisfying payoff.
* Despite its beautiful world, the narrative feels shallow. Repetitive NPC dialogue and forgettable characters make it difficult to form any emotional connection to the world.

Overall, the game is worth playing for its exceptional sense of exploration alone as few open-world games offer the same level of freedom and scale. Its engine is genuinely impressive and has the potential to set a new benchmark for the genre. If Pearl Abyss ever focuses on delivering a cohesive single-player experience instead of what often feels like a single-player MMO, the sequel could be something truly special.

TL;DR:

Overall: 7/10

Crimson Desert feels like one of the most ambitious games ever made, but also one of the most unfocused. It reaches moments where it genuinely feels like a masterpiece, only to immediately frustrate you with poor puzzle design, an awful story, clunky controls, or unnecessarily complicated systems. I never stopped admiring its world, but I frequently stopped enjoying the game itself. If the developers had focused on refining fewer systems instead of trying to include everything, this could have been one of the greatest RPGs ever made. Instead, it's an excellent open-world sandbox held back by an identity crisis.

I have very mixed feelings about this game.

At one point, it seemed like the greatest video game of all time. It had endless possibilities, vibrant open world, amazing combat, breathtaking graphics with insane draw distance, decent character customizations, pets, and much more...

Despite being so ambitious, this game lacks identity. It tries to do so many things and takes inspiration from some of our favourite video games. But we all know a game for everyone is a game for noone.

Some of the aspects this game needs HEAVY improvements:

Story: 2/10 - the only good thing about the story is the voice acting, everything else sucks. I can't even be bothered to tell you how annoying bad it is
Controls: 4/10 - it never stops feeling better, you will get used to the controls but never really love it
Combat: 7/10 - feels good againts mobs of enemies and some bosses are really fun. But so many bosses in this game have the most horrific design in the history of video games. 
Puzzles: 0/10 - I don't even remember the amount of times I had to search youtube for stupid ♥♥♥♥. No puzzle in this game is innovative or fun. Almost everything is a puzzle and it is super tiring. These devs should never be allowed to design another puzzle and I am so dead serious. This aspect is what killed the game for me mostly.
Menus: 5/1…

I recommend Crimson Desert, but not because of the story. While it's decent, I've played plenty of RPGs with much stronger storytelling. What really makes this game stand out is the incredible world, stunning graphics, and the amount of effort the developers keep putting into it through constant updates.

The scenery is absolutely breathtaking, and the game can easily push your PC to its limits. Whether you're exploring, fighting, or just taking in the views, there's always something to keep you engaged.

Pros: 
- Massive Open World Sandbox Game.
- Great Graphics. I found myself mesmerized from everything from the landscape to trees. 
- Immersive and lively world.
- Fun Combat, which you're able to change the difficulty to fit your playstyle.
- Overwhelming amount that you can do in the game.
- 3 Playable Characters.
- Replayability. 
- Loads of Puzzles. (If you enjoy them)
- Frequent updates from the developer, and they have consistently listened to players' feedback.

Cons:
- Story was lack luster.
- Repetitive fetch quests whenever you interact with a new vendor. I eventually just stopped doing them.
- Too many bounties and far away from drop off points in each territory. I eventually stopped doing them as well.
- Inability to share abyssal cubes (skill points) across characters. So I didn't end up playing Oonkga or Damiane much at all. 
- Controls while improved, can still be a pain in the butt.
- Exploring the vast world of Pywel felt daunting at times, given the great scale of the map.
- As someone that explores an area in its entirety before progressing the main story, I found many instances where it felt like the game wanted me to prioritize the main missions over the exploration and side quests because I would frequently find items and say to myself "I could have used that item way back when." Like a cloak with high Frost Resistance which would have came in handy in Pailune, but I found it in the middle of the Crimson Desert.

If you're like me, you've purchased many hyped games over the years only to go back to your "main game" after a short play session or two with the new hotness.  As a result, I skip most of what comes out these days.  Prior to release, I was looking for something to put my new hardware through its paces and the more I read about Crimson Desert, the more intrigued I was.  In the end, I decided to give it a try and went in with very little expectations.

The first thing that surprised me was how much fun I had (once past the tutorial content) and continued to have beyond the first play session.   It obviously looks good and sounds good.  The world is massive so if you're on hunt for an open-world experience, there's tons to explore.  It really was just the right mix or blend of what the game brought to the table that held my interest.

The game isn't perfect (what game is nowadays?).  People griped about the story and I can see why.  If that makes or breaks a game for you then read some other reviews out there before pulling the trigger.  It was a little clunky at times, but I felt there was a variety of options to have fun where it didn't bother me much.  I enjoyed seeing the camp come together.  Many of the complaints players had about various in-game systems (such as storage and its location) have been patched multiple times and improved.  

It was an ambitious project.  I'm glad they attempted it and continue to improve upon it.  No regrets on my purchase or the time spent.  Looking forward to seeing what else they cook up in time.

Ultimately, the dopamine you get from this game is a numb kind. The gear you get is essentially just cosmetic, the combat can be reduced down to one button attacks, dodging/ parry and spamming food. 

Even with all that said the world is huge, and good looking on the right settings.

With enough time spent you can find a rhythm that is enjoyable.

citations.review_text:
A massive open world sandbox inspired by Black Desert Online (BDO). Veterans of BDO will appreciate the nods and even a few boss cameos sprinkled through the games story. It's a mix many open world games, most notably Assassins Creed, Red Dead Redemption 2 and of course BDO. It's the classic tale of heroes VS. Bandits and the story itself is about as interesting as an ingredient list on a box of cereal but for people who have played BDO this is par for the course and nothing unexpected. 

After finishing the main story I enjoyed my 200+ hours of gameplay but there are some major gripes that I had going through this game.

1. I strongly disliked Kliff and had to resort to mods to make going through 200+ hours possible. Why the developer locked the protagonist is beyond me.

2. Locking out the other 2 playable characters intermittently during gameplay. People want freedom to sandbox in a sandbox game not rules imposed by a script.

3. Third person camera was janky and difficult to control at times and in certain environments such as tight spaces and certain boss fights.

Overall I'd give it a solid 8/10 and worth your time and money if you're into this sort of thing. It's too bad that with all that time and money spent the developer couldn't actually make a memorable story or memorable characters to go along with all that flashy combat and environment detail. Wide as an ocean, shallow as a puddle.
Great game. The best world building I have seen in a very long time. Main character falls a little flat in the story, but the exploration and many game mechanics more than make up for it.

If you're like me, you've purchased many hyped games over the years only to go back to your "main game" after a short play session or two with the new hotness.  As a result, I skip most of what comes out these days.  Prior to release, I was looking for something to put my new hardware through its paces and the more I read about Crimson Desert, the more intrigued I was.  In the end, I decided to give it a try and went in with very little expectations.

The first thing that surprised me was how much fun I had (once past the tutorial content) and continued to have beyond the first play session.   It obviously looks good and sounds good.  The world is massive so if you're on hunt for an open-world experience, there's tons to explore.  It really was just the right mix or blend of what the game brought to the table that held my interest.

The game isn't perfect (what game is nowadays?).  People griped about the story and I can see why.  If that makes or breaks a game for you then read some other reviews out there before pulling the trigger.  It was a little clunky at times, but I felt there was a variety of options to have fun where it didn't bother me much.  I enjoyed seeing the camp come together.  Many of the complaints players had about various in-game systems (such as storage and its location) have been patched multiple times and improved.  

It was an ambitious project.  I'm glad they attempted it and continue to improve upon it.  No regrets on my purchase or the time spent.  Looking forward to seeing what else they cook up in time.

This is by far the best open-world adventure game I've played in a very long time!  While the controls took a little getting used to, I am glad I stuck with it and now enjoy playing this game every day.  The amount of detail is spectacular, the crisply-rendered detail so far away makes me sometimes just pause to take in the view.  The combat is exciting and satisfying, and exploration is rewarded with the discovery of secrets and puzzles.  I can't wait to see what Pearl Abyss does next!

At one point, it seemed like the greatest video game of all time. It had endless possibilities, vibrant open world, amazing combat, breathtaking graphics with insane draw distance, decent character customizations, pets, and much more...

Despite being so ambitious, this game lacks identity. It tries to do so many things and takes inspiration from some of our favourite video games. But we all know a game for everyone is a game for noone.

Some of the aspects this game needs HEAVY improvements:

Story: 2/10 - the only good thing about the story is the voice acting, everything else sucks. I can't even be bothered to tell you how annoying bad it is
Controls: 4/10 - it never stops feeling better, you will get used to the controls but never really love it
Combat: 7/10 - feels good againts mobs of enemies and some bosses are really fun. But so many bosses in this game have the most horrific design in the history of video games. 
Puzzles: 0/10 - I don't even remember the amount of times I had to search youtube for stupid ♥♥♥♥. No puzzle in this game is innovative or fun. Almost everything is a puzzle and it is super tiring. These devs should never be allowed to design another puzzle and I am so dead serious. This aspect is what killed the game for me mostly.

Pros: 
- Massive Open World Sandbox Game.
- Great Graphics. I found myself mesmerized from everything from the landscape to trees. 
- Immersive and lively world.
- Fun Combat, which you're able to change the difficulty to fit your playstyle.
- Overwhelming amount that you can do in the game.
- 3 Playable Characters.
- Replayability. 
- Loads of Puzzles. (If you enjoy them)
- Frequent updates from the developer, and they have consistently listened to players' feedback.

Cons:
- Story was lack luster.
- Repetitive fetch quests whenever you interact with a new vendor. I eventually just stopped doing them.
- Too many bounties and far away from drop off points in each territory. I eventually stopped doing them as well.
- Inability to share abyssal cubes (skill points) across characters. So I didn't end up playing Oonkga or Damiane much at all. 
- Controls while improved, can still be a pain in the butt.
- Exploring the vast world of Pywel felt daunting at times, given the great scale of the map.
- As someone that explores an area in its entirety before progressing the main story, I found many instances where it felt like the game wanted me to prioritize the main missions over the exploration and side quests because I would frequently find items and say to myself "I could have used that item way back when." Like a cloak with high Frost Resistance which would have came in handy in Pailune, but I found it in the middle of the Crimson Desert.

Overall Crimson Desert is stupid levels of fun and I believe Pearl Abyss have truly set a new standard for the open world genre.
Great graphics and gameplay. Controls abit awkward. Would recommend. Random crashes initially appears to be fixed since recent patches

Crimson Desert gives me so many things vanilla Skyrim never could give me. It's a finished Game and the developers are still pumping more content into it. Which is crazy....

Sure, the controls can be pretty clunky at times, the puzzles can be absolutely nerve-wracking and the story is honestly mid. But besides that, the game is just off the charts.

The armor customization alone has set a new gold standard for me. The amount of freedom is incredible. You can dye and refine a badass looking sword or you can make a stick into the mightiest weapon, it's your choice.

And then there are the pets. Cats, badgers, raccoons, a baby wyvern, and even a mechanical eagle. I spent hours grinding just to get my cat a running wheel, and the best part is that the grind was actually fun because it unlocked so many other new options along the way.

What I love most is that Crimson Desert does not force you too hard into the main story just to make progress. After the first chapter, you can simply start adventuring for hours, days, or even weeks, and the world keeps rewarding your curiosity.

It is a pearl (pun intended) with some mud on it but it is a big, shiny one.

For me, this is Game of the Year. After more than 200 hours, I am still curious about so many things in this world, and that is exactly what makes it amazing.

Wait for this one to be on sale unless they fix some of the more glaring problems that make the experience frustrating. That being said, what the game does well it does very very well.
